{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Auy12LnJ91WQNTS3AQvFCq","type":"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the full schema for the SQLite database at `/app/oewn.sqlite`. It appears to be the **Open English WordNet (OEWN)** database. Below is a summary of all tables and their structure:\n\n---\n\n**Core Lexical Data**\n\n- `words` — base word forms (`wordid`, `word`)\n- `casedwords` — cased/capitalized variants of words (`casedwordid`, `wordid`, `casedword`)\n- `lexes` — lexical units/lemmas, linking words to a part-of-speech (`luid`, `posid`, `wordid`, `casedwordid`)\n- `senses` — sense entries connecting a lexical unit to a synset (`senseid`, `sensekey`, `synsetid`, `luid`, `wordid`, `casedwordid`, `lexid`, `sensenum`, `tagcount`)\n- `synsets` — synonym sets with a definition (`synsetid`, `posid`, `domainid`, `definition`)\n\n**Parts of Speech and Domains**\n\n- `poses` — part-of-speech lookup (`posid` one of `n/v/a/r/s`, `pos` label)\n- `domains` — lexicographer domain/file categories (`domainid`, `domain`, `domainname`, `posid`)\n\n**Relations**\n\n- `relations` — relation type definitions (`relationid`, `relation`, `recurses`)\n- `semrelations` — semantic relations between synsets (`synset1id`, `synset2id`, `relationid`)\n- `lexrelations` — lexical relations between specific senses (`synset1id`, `lu1id`, `word1id`, `synset2id`, `lu2id`, `word2id`, `relationid`)\n\n**Morphology and Pronunciation**\n\n- `morphs` — morphological forms (`morphid`, `morph`)\n- `lexes_morphs` — links lexical units to their morphological variants (`luid`, `wordid`, `posid`, `morphid`)\n- `pronunciations` — pronunciation strings (`pronunciationid`, `pronunciation`)\n- `lexes_pronunciations` — links lexical units to pronunciations with optional dialect variety (`luid`, `wordid`, `posid`, `pronunciationid`, `variety`)\n\n**Verb-Specific Tables**\n\n- `vframes` — verb frames (sentence patterns) (`frameid`, `frame`)\n- `vtemplates` — verb templates (`templateid`, `template`)\n- `senses_vframes` — links senses to verb frames\n- `senses_vtemplates` — links senses to verb templates\n\n**Adjective-Specific Tables**\n\n- `adjpositions` — adjective syntactic positions (`positionid` one of `a/p/ip`, `position`)\n- `senses_adjpositions` — links senses to adjective positions\n\n**Examples and Usage**\n\n- `samples` — example sentences for synsets/senses (`sampleid`, `sample`, `source`, `synsetid`, `luid`, `wordid`)\n- `usages` — usage notes (`usageid`, `usagenote`, `synsetid`, `luid`, `wordid`)\n\n**External Links**\n\n- `ilis` — ILI (Interlingual Index) identifiers (`ili`, `synsetid`)\n- `wikidatas` — Wikidata entity identifiers (`wikidata`, `synsetid`)\n\n---\n\n**Key observations:**\n\n- The `posid` column uses single characters: `n` (noun), `v` (verb), `a` (adjective), `r` (adverb), `s` (adjective satellite).\n- `luid` serves as the primary key for lexical units in the `lexes` table and is the main join key across many tables.\n- `synsetid` and `wordid` are foreign key references used extensively across tables, though no explicit `FOREIGN KEY` constraints or indexes are declared in the schema.\n- No explicit indexes are defined in the schema, which may affect query performance on large
